result.title: MINT: Meeting-time Indicators for Truncation in Multi-Step Off-Policy RL
result.comment: Accepted at NeurIPS 2026. 81 pages, 40 figures, including appendices. Code: https://github.com/seungyubhan/mint
result.summary: Many multi-step off-policy temporal-difference methods handle policy mismatch through products of per-step trace coefficients, leading to a trade-off between variance control and long-horizon signal. The maximum trace length consequently becomes a sensitive hyperparameter. We propose MINT (Meeting-time INdicators for Truncation), which replaces these products with a binary stopping indicator: one until coupled behavior and target trajectories first meet, zero thereafter. At the true value function, the indicator's idempotence yields a variance bound governed by meeting-time survival. For practical implementation, a single sampled action provides a model-free surrogate for the stopping rule, requiring no transition model or mixing-time estimate. We derive separate sufficient conditions for contraction of the state-coupled operator and its practical surrogate under fixed-policy evaluation. On MuJoCo and DeepMind Control tasks, MINT outperforms the reported multi-step baselines; the main MuJoCo comparison uses a common cap without per-task cap-length tuning. We also demonstrate the effectiveness of MINT on Atari 100k, RWRL, and OGBench experiments; MINT adapts the backup horizon to reduce target variability relative to long fixed-horizon backups across tasks and dynamics.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文提出 MINT，用行为轨迹与目标轨迹首次相遇的二值停止指示替代多步 off-policy TD 中逐步迹系数的连乘，并给出方差界与收缩条件，在 MuJoCo、Atari 100k 等上验证自适应备份长度可降低目标方差。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「相遇即截断」的自适应回撤长度与方差—长程信号权衡，可能为 latent/循环推理中如何确定 STOP 时机与截断监督视野提供可核查的线索，但不涉及视觉或多模态状态。
